![](data:image/png;base64,)

> *You press your palm against the tree's bark in the Dogwood Forest. A ring of points appears in your head. You're not sure how–but you know each one is a place you can reach. You concentrate on one of the points and take a deep breath feeling your physical body fade as your energy becomes one with the tree. You open your eyes to find you and your party are no longer standing in Dogwood Forest…*

## Summary

Wandering Trees propagate through roots running deep in the non-linear underworld. A "Mother Tree" sends out "Ramets" which burst from the ground in distant locations. A Mother and Ramets is a single connected organism.

Brave adventurers can assume the role of *Navigator* and guide their party from one tree to another. Traversing a Wandering Tree is a skill that must be learned or aided by means of magic. While travelling *Navigators* have reported spiritual insights, temporary loss of one's physical self and on occasion the presence of something ancient.

## Wandering Tree Networks

The Non-linear nature of the Wandering Tree's connections means a traditional map cannot be made or shared. Even if all the physical locations of Wandering Tree are known the pathways to travel must be learned through personal experience and can be represented in game by ring maps–visual aids that obscure the physical location of each trees in the network.

## Navigating a Network

To traverse the living connections of Wandering Trees:

1. All who wish to travel together must be in physical contact with the tree  
2. Someone volunteers as *Navigator* and connects to the tree, asking it to guide their party with its energy. This takes singular focus similar to casting a spell.  
3. A *ring map* is presented to the Navigator. The current point on the ring map is identified to players by the Warden.  
4. The Navigator chooses a point on the ring map as their destination. No restrictions exist for travelling from one point to the other–all points are considered an equal distance from eachother.  
5. The Navigator makes a WIL Save. The group becomes energy, traveling through the wandering roots arriving at their destination according to the Save results:

| WIL Save              | Results                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Success               | Travel goes smoothly. Your group arrives safely.  Navigator adds a \*\*fatigue\*\* to their inventory                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Failure               | The journey is demanding. Your group arrives safely. Navigator is \*\*deprived\*\*.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Critical Success (1)  | The Navigator connects deeply with the Mother Tree. She reveals herself to you.  Warden identifies the Mother Tree location on the ring map.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Critical Failure (20) | Something ancient and terrible has noticed you. Your blood runs cold. You lose all presence of those traveling with you. It feels like it's right behind you but you can't look...you panic: Make an additional WIL save: **Fail:** The party arrives at a random point in the network. The navigator takes d6 WIL damage.(Note: The point of arrival is shown to the players on the ring map by the Warden) **Success:** The party arrives at their desired location. The navigator is deprived |

## Creating a Wandering Network

Creating a network is the first step to introducing Wandering Trees into your game.

### Place Wandering Trees

1. Decide where to place the Mother tree on your map. Mother trees are typically in remote locations or protected and kept secret by an invested group. Label this tree "A1" on your map.  
2. Place the desired connected trees (Ramets) across your map. Aim to create new choices and opportunities for adventure with the placement of your trees. Try 3-5 for a region and 5-10 for a sprawling realm. Drop dice onto a map to determine their position if you prefer to generate random locations.  
3. Number each Ramet A2, A3, A4 etc.  
4. Flesh out the exact location and any pertinent details of each tree's location. Will someone be around to notice them arrive? What's the weather like? Is there danger? See example network below.

### Draw Ring Maps

You'll be creating a labeled map for you (the Warden) and a separate un-labelled map that you will show players when they attempt to traverse the network.

1. First draw a circle and put "A" in the centre. This is to identify the network and the orientation of your map.  
2. Draw a dot for each tree in your network on the circle.  
3. Label each dot A1, A2, A3, A4 etc. in a random order  
4. On a fresh sheet of paper draw the same circle and points but don't label them. Do write "A" in the centre to communicate the orientation and identify if there is more than one network (B, C etc.). This is what you will show to players when they are *Navigating* the network.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

### Using Your Ring Map

How you present the ring map to players is up to you. Keep your player-facing map untouched relying on players to take their own notes or draw their own ring map or simply hand the unlabeled map to players and let them hold onto it and mark it up as they please.

The Ring Map exists to introduce choices, reward exploration and introduce risk. Instantaneous long distance travel is powerful–it should come at a cost and be interesting.

## Example Wandering Tree Network

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**Eldred Region - Wandering Tree Network A.**

* A1: Deep in the Eldred Forest at the base of the Forbidden Falls  
* A2: Amongst a stand of spruce trees near an abandoned camp  
* A3: A small tree on the edge of the Cranberry bog just outside Hormwell Village  
* A4: A frail sapling kept deep underground in a Wizard's quarters.  
* A5: The singular tree in the protected courtyard of Princess Sunshadow  
* A6: Providing shade to the Gurnell family's farmhouse. Has a swing hanging from it.

## Wandering Tree Propagation

Mother trees can only be grown from seeds. The techniques for harvesting and germinating seeds is lost to time. Mention of seeds can be found in ancient texts and depicted in artwork from forest-dwelling people. There are some who claim preserved Mother seeds are hidden in tombs and kept behind lock and key in royal vaults.

It is possible to achieve artificial propagation through cuttings **but only from a Mother tree**. Wandering Trees are fickle plants and a cutting requires great care and careful tending for 6-8 weeks before rooting will occur. Once rooted the new Ramet can be used for travel.

Like any plant a Wandering Tree can succumb to disease, natural disasters or at the hand of man.

* When a Ramet is killed it can no longer be travelled through.  
* When a Mother is killed so too are its Ramets. Travelling a network is not possible without a living Mother.

## 💡Wandering Trees in Game

* Why train as a Navigator when a single lick of an underworld toad can get you the same result?  
* A new Ramet has rooted since last travelling the network...where does it lead and who propagated it?  
* Pesky cultists are suspected to be travelling an unknown Wandering tree network. Where are they coming from?  
* If only we could somehow propagate a wandering tree inside the enemy gates...  
* Where exactly is the Mother Tree and who might have originally planted it?
